messages:
Mia: Heads up — new customer NimbleHealth (org: nimble-402) cannot find any API keys after self-serve signup. They hit our /v1/responses endpoint and got a 401. They’re blocked on a PoC demo for tomorrow. @Javier @Sam :eyes:

Sam: Can you paste the exact error they see and the console screenshot? Also double-check they're looking at the correct project dropdown in Console (project scoping has bitten us before).

Mia: Screenshot attached in thread (uploaded). Error from curl they ran: 
```\ncurl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_missing\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"input": "test"}' 
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{\"error\":{\"message\":\"Invalid API key\"}}\n```
Console shows "No API keys for this project" when they select the default project. Billing shows trial credits active. Signup event id: signup_2026_03_15_9981.

Javier: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) provisioning job might have failed during post-signup key create. 2) The customer could have been auto-assigned to a non-default project due to our project selection rule. I’ll tail the provisioning logs now.

support-bot: Provisioning job queued (job_id: pj_88321) at 1769549905. Retry scheduled in 60s.

Javier: Found a failure in the provisioning service around signup_2026_03_15_9981: 
```\nERROR provisioning-service - 2026-03-15T14:18:28Z - signup_2026_03_15_9981 - Failed to create api key: permission denied: service-account-redwood@projects/infra-prod.iam - causer: iam.createKey -> 403
stack: /srv/provisioner/keys.go:142 -> /srv/provisioner/worker.go:58\n```
Looks like the infra service account lacked iam.createKey on the target project for that tenant. That would leave the org created but without a key.

Sam: If that's the case, workaround is to manually create a key and attach it to nimble-402 and mark the provisioning job as succeeded so auto-retry doesn't create duplicate keys. I can run the admin create if you give me the org id.

Mia: Org id is nimble-402. Customer contact: sara@nimblehealth.com. They need a temporary key for the demo.

Javier: I'll fix the permission on the infra SA so future signups don't fail: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding infra-prod --member=serviceAccount:service-account-redwood@infra-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin` (one-time). After that we should re-run the provisioning job.

Sam: While infra permission is being updated, creating a manual key: 
```\n# internal admin tool (run from ops vm)
/admin tools create-api-key --org nimble-402 --project default --note \"onboard temp key\"
# returns: sk_test_7Xx... (copy paste to customer)\n```
I’ll scope it to expire in 72h.

Mia: Created and emailed temp key to sara@nimblehealth.com; set expiry 72h. Customer confirmed they can call the API now and got 200. :tada:

Olivia: Good. FYI sales — they were on trial; please confirm we didn’t auto-upgrade project billing.

Javier: I patched infra permission and requeued failed provisioning job (pj_88321) at 1769549999. Job succeeded on retry and created the canonical API key for nimble-402; I disabled the temp key and rotated secrets.

Mia: Closing loop with customer: summarised root cause (missing SA role caused provisioning job failure) and steps taken. They want a confirmation email we fixed the issue and that their prod invite will have keys pre-provisioned.

Sam: Action items for follow-up: 1) Add a pre-check in provisioning to validate infra SA IAM bindings and surface an alert if missing. 2) Add monitoring to detect orgs without keys 10 minutes after signup and auto-notify #eng-oncall. 3) Postmortem if we see >1 occurrence this week.

Mia: Thanks everyone — marking resolved for now.
